Hi Ben.  You're correct that the error *can* be more serious than a  
warning, and in your case, given that ergm is not returning anything,  
it does seem like a bug.  This reminds me of another similar email to  
this list over a month ago.  I checked back, and it was from Marsela  
Dauti and dated Sept. 19, 2009.
(Sorry, Marsela, for the lack of response on that!)

Things like this would be much easier to diagnose with specific  
examples:  In particular, the most helpful thing would be to send  
enough that the email recipient can easily reproduce the error on his/ 
her own machine.  One can try to guess at how to construct such an  
example based on clues written in emails, but this takes time, and  
time is in pretty short supply for a lot of us these days.

Can you (or Marsela) send specific code that will produce this error?   
That would be most helpful, since it sounds like this may be a simple  
mistake in ergm.  Thanks in advance!

Dave

PS.  Sometimes, an "error" is more like a warning:  By using the "try"  
function as some ergm procedures do, these procedures can detect when  
something *would* cause an error and then take some alternative  
action.  But that seems like it's not what's happening here.

messages.body_plain:
Hello again,
The problem all boiled down a line of code in robust.inverse.  This
line in question reads:
        Hsvd <- svd(H)
In my call to ergm, I was (mis)using the dyadcov term in a way that
caused a row of NAs in the Hessian matrix.  This caused svd to fail.
As it so happens, this line of code has been updated in the ergm
binaries and source currently available on cran to:
     Hsvd <- try(svd(H), silent=TRUE)
The version number (2.2-1) of ergm hadn't changed from what I had
installed to the present, but there must have been some minor
modifications.  I've also noticed another issue.  When I load ergm
directly the robust.inverse function is correct (with try(svd...)
while if I load ergm via statnet, the older chunk (where svd is being
used without try) is being used for robust.inverse.  That's not an
error per se, but having statnet load an older version of ergm did
lead to some confusion.
Hopefully this is helpful to others confronting this issue.  To the
statnet team, the suite of packages rules and the documentation
(especially the JSS special edition) is great!
Ben

Hello.

I have a new question and thought I would share the answer to a  
previous question I posted and have since tracked down.

Previous question:

I sought to run an R program using R CMD BATCH as a terminal command  
from within Stata (via Stata's shell command) on Mac OS 10.6.1.  When  
I did, the R program would "break" at the point of loading Network.   
The error was "Error: package 'network' is not installed for  
'arch=x86_64'"  Those of you familiar with R may recognize it, but I  
did not.  I may not be precise in how I state this, but on the Mac,  
packages can be installed for three architectures: i386, ppc and  
x86_64. Statnet related packages install on i386 and ppc, but not  
x86_64.  My terminal defaults to x86_64, where it did not find Network  
or other Statnet packages.  I do not know how to change the default,  
but I was able to specify the architecture to use for the program's  
execution:

R --arch=i386 CMD BATCH program.r.

Again, I am probably not describing this in a technically precise way,  
but if you run R programs from the command line -- in my case Stata's  
shell command, which allows you to pass OS commands from within a  
Stata do file -- an error of the type I faced may be a mismatch of  
default arch and where your packages are installed.  Thank you to  
Magnus Thor Torfason at Columbia's b-school for pointing me in the  
right direction (a mismatch of package install locations and the  
default being used).

messages.body_plain:
Hi statnet group,

I got a response that indicated that my question was a problem that  
others have run into, so I thought I'd present my solution. I wrote a  
function that takes a network and a vector of edge attributes, and  
returns a 3 column matrix with the edgelist of the network's largest  
component plus the corresponding edge attributes. This can be easily  
read back into a network object or into tnet, a package I've been  
playing with.

Disclaimer: I am not a programmer and have self-taught myself R so I  
make no claims that this is great code but it appears to be working  
for me.Any advice on how to improve would be great! Hopefully some  
part of it might help others out there and save some time.

Second disclaimer: I wrote the function for undirected networks, if  
you're working with directed networks then you will have to change a  
few minor things.

-Michael

#largest.component.edgeattr(net, edgeattr)
#Takes a network object and a vector of edge attributes for that  
network, and returns
#an edgelist for the largest component of that network with a 3rd  
column containing
#the edge attributes;

largest.component.edgeattr <- function(net, edgeattr){

#Get edgelist from network, attach attribute
edgelist <- as.matrix.network(net, matrix.type = "edgelist",  
directed=FALSE)
edgelist <- cbind(edgelist, edgeattr)

#Initialize weighted adjacency matrix
numnodes <- network.size(net)
zeros <- rep(0, numnodes^2)
edgeattr_mat <- matrix(zeros, nrow = numnodes, ncol = numnodes)
#Add in edge weights for each tied node pair to matrix edgeattr_mat
for(x in 1:network.edgecount(net)) {
	i <- edgelist[x,1]
	j <- edgelist[x,2]
	edgeattr_mat[i,j] <- edgelist[x,3]
	#If network is undirected, symmetrize the assignments
	edgeattr_mat[j,i] <- edgelist[x,3]
	}

#Create a new edgelist for the largest subcomponent, in addition to a  
vector comp_names
	#comp_names = a crosswalk between node IDs in the largest  
subcomponent and the network such that
	#if i is the index of a node in the subcomponent, comp_nodes[i] =  
node index in the network
comp <- as.network(component.largest(net, connected="weak", result =  
"graph"), matrix.type = "adjacency", directed = FALSE)
comp_names <- as.numeric(comp %v% "vertex.names")
comp_edgelist <- as.matrix.network(comp, matrix.type = "edgelist")

#initializing edgeattr_comp = edge attributes vector for largest  
component edges
edgeattr_comp <- vector(mode = "integer",  
length=network.edgecount(comp))

#Extract the attribute for each edge in the largest subcomponent from  
edgeattr_mat above, using the
#crosswalk vector comp_names to translate node names between the two  
networks
for(x in 1:network.edgecount(comp)) {
	i <- comp_names[comp_edgelist[x,1]]
	j <- comp_names[comp_edgelist[x,2]]
	edgeattr_comp[x] <- edgeattr_mat[i,j]
	}

#comp_edgelist is the weighted edgelist
comp_edgelist <- cbind(comp_edgelist, edgeattr_comp)
return(comp_edgelist)
}

Hi statnet group,

I got a response that indicated that my question was a problem that  
others have run into, so I thought I'd present my solution. I wrote a  
function that takes a network and a vector of edge attributes, and  
returns a 3 column matrix with the edgelist of the network's largest  
component plus the corresponding edge attributes. This can be easily  
read back into a network object or into tnet, a package I've been  
playing with.

Disclaimer: I am not a programmer and have self-taught myself R so I  
make no claims that this is great code but it appears to be working  
for me.Any advice on how to improve would be great! Hopefully some  
part of it might help others out there and save some time.

Second disclaimer: I wrote the function for undirected networks, if  
you're working with directed networks then you will have to change a  
few minor things.

-Michael

#largest.component.edgeattr(net, edgeattr)
#Takes a network object and a vector of edge attributes for that  
network, and returns
#an edgelist for the largest component of that network with a 3rd  
column containing
#the edge attributes;

largest.component.edgeattr <- function(net, edgeattr){

#Get edgelist from network, attach attribute
edgelist <- as.matrix.network(net, matrix.type = "edgelist",  
directed=FALSE)
edgelist <- cbind(edgelist, edgeattr)

#Initialize weighted adjacency matrix
numnodes <- network.size(net)
zeros <- rep(0, numnodes^2)
edgeattr_mat <- matrix(zeros, nrow = numnodes, ncol = numnodes)
#Add in edge weights for each tied node pair to matrix edgeattr_mat
for(x in 1:network.edgecount(net)) {
	i <- edgelist[x,1]
	j <- edgelist[x,2]
	edgeattr_mat[i,j] <- edgelist[x,3]
	#If network is undirected, symmetrize the assignments
	edgeattr_mat[j,i] <- edgelist[x,3]
	}

#Create a new edgelist for the largest subcomponent, in addition to a  
vector comp_names
	#comp_names = a crosswalk between node IDs in the largest  
subcomponent and the network such that
	#if i is the index of a node in the subcomponent, comp_nodes[i] =  
node index in the network
comp <- as.network(component.largest(net, connected="weak", result =  
"graph"), matrix.type = "adjacency", directed = FALSE)
comp_names <- as.numeric(comp %v% "vertex.names")
comp_edgelist <- as.matrix.network(comp, matrix.type = "edgelist")

#initializing edgeattr_comp = edge attributes vector for largest  
component edges
edgeattr_comp <- vector(mode = "integer",  
length=network.edgecount(comp))

#Extract the attribute for each edge in the largest subcomponent from  
edgeattr_mat above, using the
#crosswalk vector comp_names to translate node names between the two  
networks
for(x in 1:network.edgecount(comp)) {
	i <- comp_names[comp_edgelist[x,1]]
	j <- comp_names[comp_edgelist[x,2]]
	edgeattr_comp[x] <- edgeattr_mat[i,j]
	}

#comp_edgelist is the weighted edgelist
comp_edgelist <- cbind(comp_edgelist, edgeattr_comp)
return(comp_edgelist)
}

messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] FAQ entry on ERGM with missing or sampled data
messages.body_plain:
Hi statnet users,

A frequent question on this forum is how to use "statnet" to estimate 
ERGM parameters from networks with sampled or missing data and how to 
simulate networks for the fitted models.

Here is a brief FAQ to that.

1) To represent missing entries in the adjacency matrix use a NA 
(instead of a 0 or a 1). "network" and "ergm" recognize that the dyad 
has not been observed.

e.g. Suppose y is a network object with missing values in it. You can 
set the missing via e.g.:

y[1,3] <- NA

2) To fit models, just do the regular thing.

e.g.

fit <- ergm(y ~ ...)

3) To simulate from the model conditional on the observed dyads (i.e., 
simulate only the NAs but respectful to the observed data and model) use 
the "simulate command". That is,

sim <- simulate(fit, constraints=~observed)

If you want an unconditional simulation (i.e., from the model but not 
conditional on the observed data itself) use the usual, e.g.,

sim <- simulate(fit)

I have attached some example code using Sampson's liking network among 
monks. It should be helpful.

In general, missing and sampled network methods have been embedded into 
"statnet" as seamlessly as we can.

I hope you enjoy using it :-)

Best,

Mark

Dear David,

statnet does recognize missing data on vertex attributes. For example,

[13] "Turks"    "Turks"    "Outcasts" "Outcasts" "Outcasts" "Outcasts"

However this version of the ergm() function does not adjust for missing 
data on vertex attributes - it only adjusts for missing values on the 
tie values. It is possible to do and we have worked out the statistical 
theory to do it, but have not implemented it in the public version. I 
expect it will appear in a major future release and we will communicate 
it to this forum.

Mark

list, applying as.vector to the whole thing (rather than to an  
individual element in the list, which is a column in the data.frame)  
doesn't actually do anything.

You are not the only one to have had a similar problem recently, by  
the way!

There are several ways to correct this.  Perhaps the most elegant is  
to use "scan" in place of "read.table", in which case the "as.vector"  
commands will be unnecessary, as in:

grov <- scan ("gro.txt")
etc.

But the easiest and probably the most instructive fix to your existing  
code (I'm not sure it will work, since I can't be sure I'm replicating  
your errors) would be as follows:

gro <- read.table("gro.txt")
grov <- as.vector(gro[,1])
etc.

I hope this helps.
Dave

going to assume your variables are separated by ','

dat = read.table("fileLocation",sep=',')

try help(read.table) for more details

You're then going to need to make your data frame into a matrix

dat = as.matrix(dat)

The next step would be to initiate the network object.

net = network(dat)

and then you can plot it with gplot

gplot(dat)

the network() and gplot() functions there are ALOT of different
options, far too many to read now, but look at the help files.

I hope that helps,

Sam

messages.body_plain:
Hello. I have been trying to apply ergm to? a symmetric trading data between countries.

I also have a number of binary, categorical, and continuous (quantitative) dyadic
attributes. For example, I am interested in how two countries with similar or
different gdp would form a trading tie.

To include those continuous dyadic attributes, first, I used the following line
for each attributes (gdp and distance):

table_gdp<-read.table("gdp.txt")
matrix_gdp<-data.matrix(table_gdp)
gdp<-network(matrix_gdp, directed=FALSE)

table_distance<-read.table("dist.txt")
matrix_distance<-data.matrix(table_distance)
distance<-network(matrix_distance, directed=FALSE)

Basically. gdp.txt is a country-by-country gdp matrix in which a cell consists
of gdp for country 1 multiplied by gdp for country 2.

dist.txt is a country-by-country distance matrix.

However, when I included them in ergm as follows, the output shows no significant results.

model1<-ergm(trade~edges+edgecov(gdp)+edgecov(dist))

Also, instead of making dyadic attributes as network variable as above,
I also tried to include them as matrix as follows:

table_gdp<-read.table("gdp.txt")
matrix_gdp<-data.matrix(table_gdp)

table_distance<-read.table("dist.txt")

matrix_distance<-data.matrix(table_distance)


model1<-ergm(trade~edges+edgecov(matrix_gdp) + edgecov(matrix_dist)).

Then, I got different results from the above input method where I made
dyadic attributes as network instead of matrix type. 

To summarize, I'd like know what is a correct method for using
multiple continuous or quantitative dyadic attributes. Also, if a network is directed,
can I just use dyadcov instead of edgecov, but in the same format?

Thanks.
